work.title: Shenoute: Listen

paragraphs.text: Rebuke him in his place [?]. This, again, is the way in which someone is [?]. [?] All the more so is the person among you who will say, “God will forgive those who do, or will do, those abominable deeds in his congregations after they have acquired all this knowledge and heard all these words.”

For it is easier, O people who have wanted this because of the impurity of their souls, for the one telling you these things to be of one mind with tax collectors, sexually immoral people, and all evildoers, if they turn away from their unjust or defiling deeds, than to be of one mind with you, because you are turning away from purity and truthful deeds toward defilement and deceitful deeds.

Was it not, rather, out of overwhelming indignation at those who had also committed corrupt deeds before today that I said these words on a day of distress, while we were gathered together: “Am I to assemble or offer an offering with impure people who commit corrupt deeds?”
Or how difficult is it for someone who speaks the truth to assemble with tax collectors, prostitutes, and all the wicked, or to offer the offering with them?

[?] because they have not turned away from their evil deeds, or rather because they did not turn away from them, but because no judgment rests upon him if he assembles or offers an offering with them. For they had not been exposed to him so that he could question them about these things.

How, on the other hand, will the matter not weigh heavily upon someone to whom people have been exposed, if he assembles with impure people who commit corrupt deeds among them, or offers offerings with them, while their blood and their judgment rest upon him?

Rather, let us say that their judgment and their blood rest upon the assembly, because not only is the soul of the one in charge of them not in agreement with those who commit that evil among us, but an obligation is also laid upon him by the ordinance and the decision decreed by God, as it has been from the beginning until now, not to let him eat bread or drink water or gather with the whole congregation to pray or present the offering until he has brought their judgment upon their heads, their blood upon their own midst.
if a person again dares to commit such abominable deeds in the Lord’s congregations, among the holy brothers who keep themselves from every defilement and every deceitful deed.

You will not, congregation, again be in turmoil, with retreats and harsh measures, as has often happened within you—either this time or during the remaining days that the one speaking with you will spend alive. Rather, those who are revealed to him as having committed corrupt deeds within you he will exclude from you, without turmoil and without shouting.

And if there are others within you who deceitfully commit abominable deeds without being known to us, whether male or female, great or small, they are left in the hands of God’s wrath, for him to punish them in his anger.

For anyone whom you do not know to be committing corrupt deeds within you—the curses written in the Scriptures and the curses in the books written for us themselves know them, to deal with them and all their sufferings. [?] the belts and bandages that this man laid aside after they had been tied around him, because they had not helped him, or had become useless, or had no use, as you will see some of them in one condition at one time, and another portion in another condition, another portion like this, and another portion like that, so that you may understand, brothers, that this man did not wrap himself in so many belts or bandages for any other reason than the matter that he himself knows about.

If the bandages or belts that have worn out, so that they are no longer useful to me or suitable for wrapping myself in during the illness in my body—or the body—are numerous in the eyes of the one who knows their number, the belts or bandages that you will see lying discarded, with no use left in them, are more numerous than those that have become useless. Yet they will seem few to you, because their ruined appearance makes it impossible to tell which is which, or this one from that one, so that someone could count them or state their number.

And they will be in the place [?]—I myself do not know who it is—who hid them there beneath the earth, in the place where the abyss, or the abysses, opened, filled with every useless thing, until the time when you see them with your own eyes.

For everything that this man who is speaking with you, congregation, did before today, he did because he wished to remove the disgrace from those committing these corrupt deeds among us and turn it upon himself, because he loves his neighbor as himself,
But now he himself is removing it from himself and turning it back upon everyone who does or will do abominable things deceitfully or secretly, whether male or female.
And their shame is upon them, for it rests upon them and is plainly visible upon them, and they are exposed as having it upon them.
and to honor them as well in the face of this. Now what is distressing is to give them a single blow. In particular, a rod of carob wood in his hand from today onward is a disgrace to him too.

These words are not directed at the brothers who are worthy of esteem, or the children who deserve love because of their purity and their love for God. Rather, they concern those from whom this holy place gains no benefit and who gain no benefit from it, because they are destroying their hope, as we said before.
Were not these places, or every congregation gathered in them because of God's name, called holy places?
Then how cursed will those be who defile them with shameful deeds!
Or was this saying not enough for those miserable wretches, when it cut them off from life once and for all: “The children who have become defiled are not his”?
Or is there still greater wrath than this that God will bring upon whoever destroys his temple: “Whoever destroys God's temple, God will destroy him”?

What is easy [?] concerning those who fear God in these congregations—how could he honor them, or how could he bless them, beyond what the saints said: “Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways”?
You will eat the fruits of your labors.

But what is distressing, again, concerning those who continually commit abominable deeds in these congregations—how will he put them to shame? even more than what the saints said in anger: “The one who does not fear God will remain in desert places forever, with no one coming to look for him.”

A man whom those living within you, O congregation, have often heard swearing, “I would rather die, or have God call me to account, than hear that someone [?] committed corrupt deeds within you, it is not evident that he is free of this judgment and the blood of those who distress him, because they were not ashamed to commit those abominable, godless deeds within you.
Oh, what will this place do?
Where will this place go?

Before today, the one who knows, or those who know the extent, or those who have measured the evil deeds they committed within you [?] will say [?]. They have finished saying that they have reached the portions of what they did, or rather that these things have overwhelmed them like a great flood, and that they themselves have drowned in it like animals, while God found us in it in his mercy.

Now, however, at this present time, those who measure it or take its measurements will say, or are saying, that it reaches the knees [?], and yet it does not reach as far as [?]. [?] And those who fell into it, or down upon it, sank up to their thighs.
Indeed, it is not like that within you now either.
May it never happen!
Nor was there much of it.

But those who fell into it wallowed in it like pigs, so that it did not merely reach their thighs, nor did they merely sink up to their thighs, but they appeared smeared and wallowing in it, from the soles of their feet to the hair on their heads.

Indeed, if that mire were deeper at this present time, or if it still reached the thighs according to its former measurements, those who saw the people who had fallen into it would say, “Certainly they could not stand up or get out of it [?], because it is so deep.”
And whoever says that it has not diminished very, very greatly is like someone who sheds blood, because he has insulted the grace that the Lord Jesus Christ has shown us.
But in the final period, in turn, they would not say that the mud reached the ankles, or the knees, or the thighs, but the necks of those who do corrupt deeds in it, whether male or female.

And again, this other expression, “measure” or “take measurements,” is not only written at the beginning of the first sheet set down from the outset, measuring or taking measurements of what exists or what has happened within you or to you, O synagogue; it is also there again: For those who came to learn or see what happened to you in the deep and hidden places, which are full of darkness—or which are dark within you—have taken account of what you did not know, what it was, and have taken account of the one who sent you.

But if someone asks, “What are these measurements, or this measuring?” or “Who are those who took measurements?” or “What did they measure?” let him tell us, or let him tell me: by what means was the house of the Lord in Jerusalem measured with a reed? and who measured it, and why they measured it or marked out its boundaries. Was it, then, in sorrow?

Or, if not, why such great reassurance? And again, on what grounds did the prophet Zechariah say, “I will take two staffs for myself, calling one Beauty and calling the second Cord”? And Was it, then, in mercy and compassion, or rather in anger and wrath, that he said afterward, “I will take my beautiful staff and throw it away, to dissolve the covenant that I established with all the peoples”?

“And they will be scattered in those days, and the Canaanites will bring out the sheep that trust in me, for it is the word of the Lord.” Then again: “I threw away the second staff, Measuring Line, to dissolve the covenant between Judah and Jerusalem.”
And again, whether in consolation or rather in rebuke, Micah the prophet also said: “They measured out my people's portion with a measuring line for a field.”

And whether those who measured that region were people from God, like the one who measured the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, and in accordance with the designation of the two staffs, Beauty and Measuring Line, which we mentioned earlier—or, instead, outsiders.
